standard_prerequisites.name: Site, sheaf of commutative R-algebras, complexes of O-modules
standard_prerequisites.statement: A site C with a sheaf of commutative R-algebras O and the derived category D(O) of complexes of O-modules.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the setting of the statement (source lines 6204-6206).

standard_prerequisites.name: Derived tensor product with a fixed complex
standard_prerequisites.statement: The functor - tensor^L_E K^bullet : D(E,d) to D(O) of the earlier lemma (the author's lemma-tensor-with-complex-derived, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the functor whose induced maps on Hom and Ext are described (statement, source lines 6208-6211).

standard_prerequisites.name: Global derived hom and its cohomology
standard_prerequisites.statement: The global derived hom introduced in the Cohomology on Sites chapter, whose cohomology modules compute Ext over O (declared as a tagged source pointer).
standard_prerequisites.use: It identifies the right hand side of the arrow (source lines 6226-6229).

standard_prerequisites.name: Derived restriction and property (P) computations
standard_prerequisites.statement: The derived Hom realised through the restriction bimodule, invariant under replacing M and N by property-(P) dg E-modules, computed as a dg Hom of bimodules (the author's lemmas lemma-functoriality-derived-restriction and lemma-compute-derived-restriction, and the section section-restriction, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: They identify the left hand side and justify the replacement (source lines 6230-6243).

core_obligations: Identify the two sides: recognise the right hand side as the global derived hom with the correct cohomology, and the left hand side as the chapter's derived Hom with the correct cohomology (source lines 6226-6234).

Reduce to property (P): replace M and N by quasi-isomorphic property-(P) dg E-modules, which leaves the left side unchanged and turns the derived tensor product into the ordinary one, and rewrite the left side as a Hom in the dg category of bimodules (source lines 6234-6243).

Build the map of complexes: use the dg functor - tensor_E K^bullet and the fact that the derived functor is computed by it on property-(P) modules to obtain a map of complexes of R-modules between the two Hom complexes (source lines 6243-6260).
Compose with the comparison map: use the canonical map from a dg Hom into the global derived Hom to obtain the promised canonical map in D(R) (source lines 6260-6273).

proof_roadmap.step: Identify the right hand side with the global derived hom and the left hand side with the chapter's derived Hom.
Reduce to property-(P) modules and rewrite the left side as a Hom in the dg category of bimodules.
Use the dg tensor functor to obtain a map of complexes of R-modules.
Compose with the canonical comparison map into the global derived hom and conclude.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-upgrade-tensor-with-complex-derived at source lines 6202-6224: for a site with a sheaf of commutative R-algebras O and a complex K^bullet of O-modules, the derived tensor functor of the earlier lemma induces a canonical map from the derived Hom over the endomorphism dg algebra E = RHom(K^bullet,K^bullet) to the derived Hom over O, which on cohomology is the map of Ext groups induced by the functor. The proof at source lines 6226-6274 has to identify the two sides (the global derived Hom of the Cohomology on Sites chapter on the right, the chapter's own derived Hom realised as a restriction bimodule on the left), reduce to dg modules with property (P) so that the derived tensor product is computed by the ordinary one, obtain a map of complexes of R-modules out of the dg Hom categories, and compose it with the canonical comparison map from a dg Hom into the global derived Hom. It is bookkeeping rather than depth, but the two identifications are exactly what makes the statement non-obvious.
